html:
Germany became a single state in 1871, when the King of Prussia was proclaimed German Emperor in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles, after victory over France. It was divided after the Second World War, from 1949 to 1990, and reunited in 1990.

For centuries the German lands had been hundreds of states inside the Holy Roman Empire. After Napoleon ended it in 1806, Prussia and Austria competed to lead them. Prussia's chief minister Otto von Bismarck won through three short wars, against Denmark, Austria and France, and built a German Empire without Austria.

Phases:

  • 1871 to 1918: the empire, which grew fast into Europe's leading industrial power, with strong science, universities and the first state social insurance.
  • 1914 to 1918: defeat in the First World War, the fall of the Kaiser.
  • 1919 to 1933: the Weimar Republic, hit by hyperinflation in 1923 and the Depression after 1929.
  • 1933 to 1945: Hitler's Nazi dictatorship, which started the Second World War in Europe and murdered six million Jews in the Holocaust.
  • 1949 to 1990: division into a democratic West Germany and a communist East Germany, with Berlin split by a wall from 1961.

West Germany's economy recovered fast in the 1950s, and it became a founding member of what became the European Union. The fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 led to reunification in 1990. Germany has since been the largest economy in Europe.

Germany also gave the world much of its science before 1933, from Einstein to the chemists of its great firms; many of its scientists, Jewish ones above all, fled the Nazis.
